To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a lattice composed with flexible momentum-compaction modules has a smaller systematic stop-band width, smaller dispersion excursion, and better chromatic properties than the conventional focusing-defocusing lattice.

a lattice composed entirely of flexible-momentum-compacting modules has a negative momentum-compacting factor and that this lattice has a small dispersion excursion and small dispersion at the center of the lattice.
we developed a flexible lattice design that has a tunable momentum-compaction factor and that can be used in medium-energy accelerators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a flexible momentum-compaction lattice for the medium-energy synchrotron.
the development of a new method of accelerator lattice design.
the design of a lattice that is flexible in the sense that its momentum-compaction factor can be varied from a negative to a positive value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flexible momentum compaction lattice is superior in many aspects to the FODO lattice, especially in medium-energy accelerators.
a lattice composed entirely of such modules has better chromatic and dynamic properties than a FODO lattice.

a flexible momentum-compaction lattice composed of the basic flexible module can be used for a wide class of medium-energy accelerators, such as the Advanced Photon Source (APS), the Advanced Light Source (ALS), and the Next Linear Collider (NLC).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flexible momentum-compaction lattice is the most promising candidate for medium-energy synchrotrons.
the dispersion of the lattice can be minimized to be the minimum of the FODO lattice containing the same number of FODO cells, while keeping the same phase advance of the basic module.
a lattice composed entirely of these modules has the best chromatic properties among all known lattice structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dispersion of the basic flexible-momentum-compacting module can be minimized, and thus a lattice composed of these modules can have excellent chromatic properties.
it is possible to design a lattice with negative momentum-compaction that has smaller dispersion excursion than an equivalent FODO lattice.
a lattice with negative momentum compaction can be designed to have the same dispersion as a lattice with positive momentum compaction.
